habitat: Usually montane and hilly country, wandering far for food. It forages alone and gathers where there is carrion.
summary: A common, localised resident. Black, with a white nape only, and a very heavy white-tipped bill. In flight it looks broad-winged, with a short tail. The call is a falsetto kraak, sometimes with deeper notes. The Newman family text says the sexes are alike and immatures are similar to adults. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Cape Crow is entirely glossy black and has a slighter bill. White-necked Raven has the white nape and the heavy white-tipped bill.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^2=4 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 2–8.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

calls.description: A falsetto kraak, although deeper notes are sometimes uttered. The texts do not separate the sexes. Grade A from the Aberdeen Plain, Eastern Cape. The filename is White-necked ravens calling.
